strengths: Clear problem motivation with effective empirical analysis showing block feature redundancy across diffusion timesteps
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple state-of-the-art models (Open-Sora, Open-Sora-Plan, Latte) with diverse metrics and ablation studies
Practical, training-free method with no architectural modifications, achieving 2.24× speedup while maintaining visual quality
Consistent improvements over recent baselines (PAB, TeaCache) with statistical significance testing and confidence intervals
Thorough ablations examining threshold sensitivity, reuse intervals, and periodic recomputation effects
Strong visual results demonstrating quality preservation across diverse video content and generation parameters
Scaling experiments with multiple GPUs showing method generalizes across different parallelization strategies
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contribution is straightforward application of similarity-based caching to DiT blocks, extending prior work (PAB, TeaCache) with modest modifications
Insufficient theoretical justification: no analysis of why L1 distance is optimal, lack of theoretical grounding for threshold mechanism, and ad-hoc choices (e.g., R/2 for recomputation)
Task-dependent hyperparameter tuning required: similarity threshold δ varies significantly across models/scenarios without principled selection guidelines, limiting practical applicability
Incomplete analysis of empirical results: improvements over TeaCache sometimes marginal with overlapping confidence intervals; dramatic reuse rate variations (Figure 6) lack explanation
Narrow baseline comparisons: only compared against PAB and TeaCache; missing comparisons with quantization, distillation, or other acceleration paradigms
Limited experimental scope: single GPU type tested, only video generation domain explored, no human evaluation studies, unclear generalization to proprietary models
Missing design justification: no comparison of global vs. block-specific thresholds, limited analysis of why reuse from all blocks is optimal, insufficient exploration of failure cases
Reproducibility concerns: no code availability mentioned, incomplete specification of model versions and baseline implementation details
Insufficient failure analysis: no discussion of content types or scenarios where method degrades more, missing robustness analysis to distribution shifts
Presentation gaps: connection between block feature variations and perceptual quality assumed rather than established, cache recomputation strategy insufficiently motivated

strengths: Addresses a practical and important problem of accelerating video diffusion model inference
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (Open-Sora, Open-Sora-Plan, Latte) with diverse video specifications
Thorough ablation studies examining threshold sensitivity, reuse rates, and reuse intervals
Provides empirical analysis of block feature dynamics through visualization and L1 distance aggregation
Demonstrates training-free applicability and multi-GPU scaling capability
Includes statistical significance testing in appendix for result validation
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Core idea of L1-based similarity threshold for caching is straightforward and incremental over existing methods (PAB, TeaCache, DeepCache)
Heuristic threshold selection without principled approach; authors acknowledge needing future work on dynamic threshold adjustment
Quality-speed tradeoff poorly analyzed: Noticeable VBench drops (e.g., 80.88→78.28% on Latte) glossed over as 'comparable'
Weak theoretical justification for why blocks with similar L1 distances should be reusable without quality degradation
Simplistic similarity metric: L1 distance used without ablation or comparison to alternatives; no justification provided
Inconsistent improvements: PAB sometimes outperforms BWCache in visual quality (Table 1) despite similar speedup claims
Limited experimental scope: Only A800 GPU tested, prompts solely from Open-Sora gallery, unclear generalization
Periodic recomputation strategy (Section 3.4) poorly motivated; interval R selection appears ad-hoc
Reproducibility concerns: No explicit code release mentioned, threshold selection pipeline incompletely specified
Missing comparisons with recent acceleration methods (FORA, SmoothCache cited but not compared)

strengths: Clear problem motivation with compelling analysis of feature redundancy in DiT blocks across timesteps
Exceptionally comprehensive evaluation across multiple models (Open-Sora, Open-Sora-Plan, Latte), diverse video configurations, and extensive metrics (VBench, LPIPS, SSIM, PSNR)
Significant and consistent practical results: 2.24× speedup with maintained or improved visual quality, scaling validated across multiple GPUs
Thorough experimental design including 1600+ video generations, ablation studies on threshold/intervals/recomputation strategies, and statistical significance testing
Training-free approach that is practically applicable to multiple models without architectural modifications
Solid technical execution with careful handling of critical denoising stages and periodic recomputation to prevent latent drift
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: core contribution is straightforward application of known caching techniques with threshold-based feature reuse to DiTs
Threshold selection requires manual tuning with no principled guidance for new tasks/models; paper acknowledges need for dynamic threshold adjustment in future work
Missing comprehensive comparisons with alternative acceleration methods (distillation, pruning, quantization); comparison limited primarily to caching-based approaches (PAB, TeaCache)
Insufficient theoretical justification for why feature L1 distance is appropriate for cache decisions; limited analysis of when/why method succeeds or fails
Incomplete characterization of failure modes: feature variation analysis shown only for 2 prompts; missing detailed exploration of content types where quality degrades significantly
Latency evaluation limited to high-end A800 GPUs; unclear how method transfers to consumer hardware, mobile deployment, or other optimization frameworks
Ad-hoc design of periodic cache recomputation strategy (Section 3.4) lacks strong theoretical grounding; practical guidelines for hyperparameter tuning across new models insufficient

strengths: Thorough empirical analysis of block-level feature dynamics across five video diffusion models with clear U-shaped pattern discovery providing solid foundation for the approach

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with 1000+ videos per model, multiple quality metrics (VBench, LPIPS, SSIM, PSNR), extensive ablation studies, multi-GPU scaling, and statistical significance testing
Training-free plug-and-play method directly applicable to existing pre-trained models without requiring architectural modifications or retraining, addressing practical deployment bottleneck
Consistent empirical improvements over baselines (1.6-2.6× speedup with comparable or better visual quality) demonstrated across diverse models and generation tasks
Well-structured presentation with clear visualizations, comprehensive supplementary material including parameter guidelines, memory analysis, and dynamic scenario evaluation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—core contribution (using average L1 distance to trigger block-wise caching) is relatively straightforward and incremental over TeaCache and PAB, primarily differing in granularity rather than conceptual advance

Similarity indicator lacks strong justification: no comparison with alternative metrics (L2, cosine similarity), arbitrary averaging across blocks rather than exploring weighted or conditional combinations, and heuristic threshold selection requiring model-specific tuning

Known latent drift problem (Section E.3, Figure 14) acknowledged but not deeply resolved; periodic recomputation is mitigation rather than solution, and cumulative drift effects on long sequences not thoroughly analyzed
Non-negligible computational overhead of cache indicator computation (10.6-22.5% of inference time, Table 13) reduces effective speedup; limited exploration of optimizations

Inconsistent performance across architectures—TeaCache achieves 4.41× on Open-Sora-Plan while BWCache achieves 2.24× due to early-stage feature oscillations with PNDM sampler, revealing robustness limitations to different noise schedules

Parameter tuning requirements weaken 'plug-and-play' claim—threshold δ requires model-specific selection from ranges (0.1-0.25), contradicting training-free advantage and requiring iterative validation

Limited theoretical grounding—frequency domain explanation for U-shaped pattern is superficial, and why block-wise caching is fundamentally better than timestep-wise lacks rigorous justification beyond empirical observation

Generalization concerns—method specific to transformer-based video diffusion; Appendix E.2 shows different patterns for image generation and class-conditional generation; unclear applicability to U-Net or other architectures

strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation across 5 major DiT-based models with extensive ablations and multi-GPU scaling experiments
Well-motivated analysis of U-shaped feature variation patterns across diffusion timesteps, validated consistently across diverse models
Training-free and broadly applicable approach with no architectural modifications required
Generally strong visual quality metrics (LPIPS, SSIM, PSNR) compared to TeaCache and PAB baselines
Thorough presentation with extensive appendix including statistical testing, memory analysis, and dynamic video evaluation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contribution is changing caching granularity from timestep to block level—an engineering choice rather than fundamental advance
Simplistic similarity indicator (Eq. 7): merely averaging L1 distances with a threshold lacks principled justification or theoretical grounding
Inconsistent performance across models: TeaCache outperforms BWCache on Open-Sora-Plan (4.41× vs 2.24× speedup), suggesting the method is not robust to different training procedures
Requires model-specific hyperparameter tuning with different δ ranges per model (Table 15), contradicting the 'plug-and-play' claim

Significant unresolved practical issues: 40-57% memory overhead (Table 11) limits applicability, latent drift problem (Section E.3) is observed but not addressed, and vague guidance on block subset selection
Unfair baseline comparisons: Skip-DiT only tested on one model, ProfilingDiT/TaylorSeer compared on extremely short videos (9-17 frames) due to OOM constraints
No theoretical analysis of when/why block-level caching outperforms timestep-level, or principled approach to setting hyperparameters without trial-and-error

strengths: Clear, well-motivated analysis of block-level feature dynamics with consistent U-shaped patterns across 5 different video diffusion models, explaining ~70% of inference latency
Practical training-free method that is plug-and-play compatible with existing pre-trained models without requiring retraining

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation: 5 models, 6+ baselines, ~1,000 videos per model, multiple metrics (VBench, LPIPS, SSIM, PSNR), ablation studies, multi-GPU scaling, and statistical significance testing
Superior quality-efficiency trade-offs: BWCache achieves better visual quality than TeaCache while maintaining competitive latency, demonstrating advantages of block-wise over timestep-wise caching
Adaptive mechanism that naturally adjusts caching aggressiveness based on scene dynamics—static content receives more aggressive caching while dynamic content is conservatively handled
Excellent presentation with clear motivation, well-organized methodology, comprehensive appendices, honest discussion of limitations, and good visual communication
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contribution is incremental—applying block-level granularity to established feature caching approaches; similarity indicator (mean L1 distance) is straightforward without justification for metric choice or averaging strategy

Latent drift problem inadequately addressed: Section E.3 reveals feature variations become unpredictable after cache reuse begins; periodic recomputation strategy (R=10%) appears ad-hoc, borrowed from PAB without rigorous analysis; sensitivity shown in Table 5 (quality range 79.31-80.28%)

Hyperparameter tuning undermines 'training-free' claim: requires manual threshold δ tuning for new models via 'generate samples and iteratively test'; memory constraints force 50% block subset usage for Wan 2.1/HunyuanVideo; not truly zero-cost deployment

Design choices lack rigorous justification: why restrict final k/2 steps from caching? Why average across blocks rather than per-block strategies? Why L1 vs other distance metrics? These appear reasonable but lack comparative analysis

Incomplete baseline comparisons: ProfilingDiT/TaylorSeer evaluated only on very short videos (9-17 frames) due to memory constraints, limiting fair comparison; Skip-DiT dismissed due to retraining costs rather than demonstrated inferiority

Generalization limitations: method specific to video DiTs with U-shaped patterns; image generation shows inverted L-shaped patterns (Section E.2); applicability to other diffusion architectures unclear; all tested models use similar Spatial-Temporal DiT design

Cache indicator computation overhead substantial: takes 10.6-22.5% of inference time (Table 13), which is non-negligible despite simplicity; memory overhead persistent across all models (~1.4-2.3× original, Table 11)

Missing critical analysis: which content types benefit most from caching? Why consistent performance across different architectures? Limited exploration of failure modes; claim of 'up to 2.6× speedup' emphasizes maximum while most results are 1.6-2.2×
